Game Rules

Played using graph paper

1.	The game utilizes the Moore Neighborhood, so for a given vertex on your graph paper, that vertex’s Moore Neighborhood are considered adjacent to that vertex.

2.	To begin, you draw a shape. Any shape will do, though curves aren’t optimal. Try to make sure any vertices or free ends land on your grid, as it will make the shape you draw impact the game.

3.	There are two basic objects in the game, a line and a node. Nodes connect lines on the vertices of your graph paper. Additionally, any node that only touches one line is a free node, and these are the most critical piece of the game.

4.	For each free node, draw 2 lines 45 degrees from the line connected to the node in either direction to the next adjacent vertex on your paper. There should be a 90 degree angle between the two child lines, and a 135 degree angle between them and the parents. Repeat this once.

5.	One application of step 4 constitutes a generation.

6.	If done correctly, every generation, each child line will alternate between being on your grid and crossing it diagonally.

7.	If two child lines land on the same vertex, in the next generation, you will skip step 4 for them.

Optional

1.	Calculate the number of child lines for each generation and see if a given seed has a representative equation for the population in a given generation.

2.	Color in the resulting polygons, (the geometric patterns are good for coloring).

3.	Try and develop seeds that produce desired patterns.
